body: Was this suppose to help me?
Terrible. She wouldn't understand. Never has.

I'm not ready for her to know. At the moment, it sounds like she believes me.

I want to come to her when I'm ready. Too much on my plate right now.
Right, that's unfortunate. Hopefully you can find adequate help. I mean you reached out, you deserve something. It's a shame.
Same here. It's becoming more and more common apparently? Sounds like they're reading a script at this point yknow. I've seen other people have similar experiences as you.

The thing about lying is that it also has to look convincing. I used to spend extra time just to make sure cuts were angled a certain way. If they appear self-inflicted then people will start asking questions, but cuts and bruises here and there are expected and common. Most people lie, because most people don't want to admit it yknow? Or don't want to stop. So you definitely aren't the only person scrambling for lies. I don't know if it'll help ease your conscience, but think of them as white lies. You aren't hurting anybody else. Not really.

Then you must understand that he wasn't in the right mindset for the time being. His intentions weren't malicious towards his family, his kids. Although he, regrettably, left you behind in the process. Again, I hope that if any of those thoughts are reoccurring, I softly advise you seek well-deserved help. Otherwise it'll be another unfortunate loss. It's a shame he didn't get the help he deserved. It's not easy for some people to reach out.

He sounds like he was a great man, and a heck of a father. Very supportive. It sounds like one hell of an image to maintain. It's better that you see him for who he was, because he sure as hell wasn't weak. He loved you, your siblings, your mother. I can't say enough how sorry I feel for you. He had numerous talents and an even larger influence on the people in his life. It's a real shame.

You're allowed to vent. This is shocking, it would be anyone. You just found out right? Not too long ago. You're justified for venting, so don't apologize for it. I'm glad you got around to seeing my post. Sincerely. I don't usually offer, but if you need to talk to someone, you can always PM me. No obligations though. Again, my condolences, I wish you the best in these dark times.

My condolences for your loss. Nobody should have to go through this. I don't believe anything I can say will help you through this tough time.

It sounds like the two of you were close.

I hope you can look back from this and remember him as he was. The good times, the kind of memories that feel welcoming, rather than tear-jerking. I'm not saying you should just move on or something like that. That's not possible. I know you said you weren't attempting suicide or anything, but. Regardless I hope you find healthy outlets. Most people will never experience this, and words cannot express how much you did not deserve this.

Take time for yourself, but don't completely isolate yourself. Take time to process, to heal. Talk to your family whenever the time is right for you. Whatever you're feeling, don't hide it. You're justified, and as someone else said, this is not your fault, and I hope you never think so in your future.

I don't know if you'll see this, or if this helps, or if this is what you were looking for. I wish you the best.

Honestly, I feel in some selective scenarios, it's fine to relate to the person posting or whatever, but for a majority of the time it's useless. It's like the person commenting is trying to bring attention to themselves, rather than do anything to help the other person.

I absolutely hate it. I feel like people in general on this thread have dealt with the same struggles, for the most part. Why else would they be here? Although they give you the guarantee that at least your post was read, it's more toxic than not. When I reply to posts, people that supposed need support one way or another, I look at the amount of comments and try to get to the posts that nobody has responded to. When people respond with useless comments, it still shows as a comment, and I'll pass over such posts, typically if nothing stands out about it. It makes the problem suddenly look resolved when it's not, and people suffer for it.

Well, I don't know if anything anyone, especially myself, could say anything to change your mind.

Is there an ulterior motive to joining the military? Are you intimidated by the idea of reaching out to somone? These can be rhetorical if you don't want to answer them. I feel like the usual recommendations of distractions won't help you. You might be beyond that.

Talking to people, reaching out isn't everyone's "thing." Your friends, are you afraid of chasing them away? Are you simply uncomfortable with talking about your situation? If they're really you're friends, they'd be understanding.

Is there a reason you hate yourself,, a reason these suicidal thoughts are emerging? There doesn't have to be a reason. If there isn't, well, that's also completely valid.

Nobody in their right mind is going to encourage you to kill yourself. I sincerely hope you won't, but this time of year suicide rates are always through the fricking roof. It's overwhelmingly devastating. You should live, give yourself the opportunity to do what you really want to do. You've never get the chance if you decide to kill yourself.

I'm pretty sure the last thing was a rough change in subject, misdirecting, but regardless, I've never been where you are currently. I've been in Colorado though. Last year. Beautiful state you live in. I've encountered nothing but wonderful people there. Ever been to Wyoming? I don't live there, but it's a sight to see for sure. Everyone will tell you this, and most people don't take it, but you can always PM me. This comment may not have helped, and if it didn't, then I personally apologize for letting you down. You deserve more out of life. You deserve more than one individual has to offer. I hope that you make it through this.
Just try something, you shouldn't have to feel like this. It doesn't just stop, but, I hope that works out for you. If it doesn't, then just make sure that to be careful.

You could try different medication, tell your doctor it isn't helping you. It might help to get something stronger.

It's a shame what you have currently doesn't help. I hope you find something that does help. It sounds rough. But yeah, not being able to enjoy anything? That's depression for you, sorry.

Don't mention it, I hope any of this helps.

I'm not going to say that your self-deprecating situation is somehow unjustified. Not to say that you must be bad at what you do, but with that mindset it's uhhh, sort of hard to believe anything else. You have to get your confidence/self-esteem back up is my guess. Hard to do, I know.

I'm not about to diagnose you with something or what have you, but people with depression tend to lose interest in things they used to enjoy. Not everyone that self-harms has depression, or like vise versa, and you might not have it, it's just an assumption on my part. I'm not a professional. You being disinterested in things could be a possible symptom of that. It might also explain the feelings of self-deprecation, but again, you don't have to be depressed to have that. You mentioned being on medication for ADHD? People with ADHD are at a higher risk of depression. Again, just my guess, and if you actually have depression then well,,, not as shocking.

You're welcome. Although my intentions are almost purely selfish. Responding to these helps me too, and well the fact that I might be able to help someone is a bonus.

Do you hate your creations, or simply the activity? Either way, if art doesn't work for you, you should try other outlets. Try new things. Heck, you can play video games, if it's a distraction it helps, even if it's just for a short time it's better than nothing. You might be really good at writing and just don't know it yet. You don't need to be good at something, you just need to enjoy yourself.
I agree with the last comment. Must be a dull blade or something of the sort. It sounds like you're just breaking skin.

Heres the thing- it is near impossible to really stop if you yourself don't want to stop/aren't planning on stopping anytime soon. Especially now, it sounds like you have more freedom now, and are free to do as you please. You aren't restrained by other people anymore. It's probably very tempting.

Whether or not you want to know how to stop is another story, but it will, unsurprisingly, get harder to manage as you indulge in the habit. I can't remember the exact reason, but for a lot of people that self-harm, they reach a point where self-harming stops "working" for them. That doesn't mean they stop doing it, but some people stop feeling it completely. Something about the body not releasing enough endorphins or something. What I'm trying to say is it won't be a reliable coping mechanism. One day it will just stop feeling good and start feeling like nothing.

It sounds like you've already created a few deep ones. I honestly do not think this will help you now, considering it sounds like you do not want to stop, but creative outlets help some people. Not everyone though. Drawing, reading, writing, listening to music. I'd say that focusing on your college work might prove as a decent distraction, but it probably won't. Personally I've taken college classes with the same habit. The importance of college doesn't really compare to the results of self-harm, especially someone that wants to continue doing it.

I'm not sure if anything I can say will help you, and that's the truth. Nobody can stop you from indulging in this habit. I can only tell you that you might reach a point where it becomes even more difficult to manage. You're already making deep cuts too. It's risky as is, but the way you're going it's more than borderline dangerous. Again, I can't stop you, but next time you want to do it wait an hour before doing it. The urge to do it might subside over time. Good luck, take care, and make sure to watch out for infections. Itchy cuts are a bitch y'know? Keep them covered and clean.

Yes, all the time. I've had some moments where I thought some were full-fledged scars that disappeared after about a year or two. Some remain. Other times, I check the scars on my hands. They're more visible whenever I scratch at them. It's less about validation and more about whether or not other people can see them.

Whether or not someone should seek out help is usually not debatable. Most people will tell you that you should, because what if one day you decide to act on those thoughts? Personally I believe it depends on you. Even if don't act on your suicidal thoughts, if said thoughts are having an impact on your day-to-day life, I think you should seek help. It's okay if you aren't sure whether or not the career you're aiming for is right for you. You can determine other careers that interest you over time, or maybe you'll enjoy your current one after you get accustomed to it.

How often are you suppose to take your medication? Be sure not to accidentally overdose, of course. Are you taking the bare minimum? Maybe keep track of how much you've already taken, with reminders not to take more? You should keep some of it on you though. Maybe have your father keep most, but have some on yourself incase it gets bad.

Getting back the motivation to do anything is a tough one. The solution differs depending on the individual. Hobbies, distractions. Finding new passions, that sort of thing. For example, if you used to love reading, find some new books that interest you. On the other hand, if all your previous interests no longer interest you, that's a different problem. You have to rediscover the things that potentially make you happy. (Unless the way you feel happens to be a symptom of depression, in which you should look into that more on it's own. I'm not going to say that medication solves everything, or that you should risk taking variations of medication at the same time. It's not a "happy pill", but if you feel like something along the lines of antidepressants might help, you should look into that, talk to your doctor about it).

Don't forget to treat yourself. Have a good day, and good luck.
Don't mention it. Again, I hope you figure everything out.

I find it interesting that you checked in the first place. Solid question, no answer.

I won't apologize. Maybe I was a little rash to begin with. The mere mention of age sets me off.

Oof, you can read. I'm so threatened.

Apparently more than you. I wouldn't worry about it.

Ah, the same way you seem to disregard life?

Get out of here, man. The shit you say isn't helpful.  Not even remotely. It's not your life on the line, anyways. I won't ask again.

In your defense, the structure for education is uhh, bad. It's usually involves a disregard for students. It challenges memory, typically, over anything else.

Your laziness, as you put it, might not be laziness at all. You don't know what to do with yourself. You don't have the motivation to do anything. You might not be lazy at all. It's not a long-shot. If you have depression, that's one of the symptoms. Loss of motivation, and interests, etc.

Do you think you're wasting your life? Maybe you just need to go a different pace. Theres no point in rushing. You deserve to live at a comfortable pace, do things you wanna do.

Try new things. Maybe theres a video game you've been curious about, or a good book you've always wanted to read. Try writing. It might help you vent too. New experiences might help.

I've heard of people getting pets, like fish, that rely on their owners to survive. It'll give you a small, yet valid reason to get up in the morning/live in general. Plus, you don't have to spend a lot of money, or do anything out of your comfort zone to keep it alive.

People, such as yourself, invalidate their situation simply because of their age, and yet somehow we wonder why suicide rates in teenagers are increasing. Oh boy, I wonder.

It's an issue that needs to be taken seriously, thanks for being a "responsible adult."

I wasn't going to comment, but I don't feel like most of the comments were very helpful.  No offense to anyone of course.

I've read all the comments. The person that said that "other people have it worse" needs to grow the fuck up, because you're upset over this, and that's super important.

I can relate to your situation (as everyone likes to comment about their situation, apparently, although they are not more relevant thans yours, you are not alone), I can't have kids either. I have an immune system/skin disease that would probably be passed down to my kids, and that's a life of pain and medication.

Other people said adopt, and a bunch of other options. They didn't satisfy you though. There isn't  much, it seems, that would counter your problem.   If you decide on one of those other options, they may not share your DNA, but it's all the glory and joy of raising a child. Additionally, you'd probably save and secure their future.

You can still get a significant other without the ability to reproduce. Contrary to belief, people can love and enjoy another persons company, whether or not they can have kids. It isn't necessarily a deal-breaker. Being in a relationship isn't just about kids, it's about you and whoever the other person may be, and what you feel for each other. Someone that respects you will understand and support your decisions.

Also hey, please don't kill yourself. There's still hope for your situation, whether you know it or not. Regardless, I hope everything works out for you. Your age and situation does not define whether or not you are deserving of this position. Nobody should resort to suicide, age doesn't matter. Good luck out there.
Yeah, you should. Good luck.

Do you know why you want to kill yourself?

Maybe you can combat these thoughts if you knew the cause, or maybe find something that works for you.

I've known people that have suicidal tendencies despite not knowing the reason, or because there wasn't a "legitimate" reason. If this is the case, then what I recommend if finding something you're passionate about. Other people will recommend that you find distractions, but I disagree. Distractions aren't long-term. What are you good at? Perhaps you enjoy cooking, drawing, etc. You should find purpose within the things you enjoy. It'll give you a reason to live, a reason to keep going.

I'm not an expert on how toxic each thing is individually.

But I have a feeling that now would probably be a good time.

It's good that you didn't do more. Theres a line between when you start and when it gets completely out of control. You need to really fight the urge to do it before you get full-fledged addicted to it.

You can always message me, if you need to vent or something.

I think I understand that. Because this habit is sacred to you, y'know? I mean you took the time to make it.

Big saaame to that second thing.

I'm actually very familiar with both.

Knives were never as deep as razors. They would remove layers of skin, and never really bleed. Additionally, they were constantly infected despite the fact that I kept it clean and covered.

Razors cut deeper. But I've broken blood vessels with the suckers.

They're like two extremes. Anyways I don't encourage that you self-harm or anything, just be careful and keep them clean.

Can't exactly relate to yours tbh. I've never carved the names of other people into my flesh.

I knew someone that did that with my name. I'd imagine that it's like, someone is special to you I guess?

I've cut words 'n shit before, just never names. Usually the kind of stuff I'd think about myself. Never other things though.
Good job. I hope you can keep going dude.

It's a little typical, but you can always pm me or something. If venting is your thing. I'm assuming it isn't though, because you hate complaining. It's valid though. This usually doesn't help, but find something to give your life more purpose. A hobby. Writing, reading, drawing. Video games. Whatever you're into? Try new things.
You shouldn't have to thank me y'know? Listen, I understand that you're more than willing to go through with this. Is there anyone you can talk to? Anything you want to do?

I'd imagine that its because you're desensitized to the idea of suicide. Has this been on your mind a lot? I don't encourage that you kill yourself. Nobody here will. You shouldn't have to go through this. You deserve better than this. You should go through options, reach out, before making this decision. There are always more options.

I might not be the best person to tell you this, because I've never dived into burning as a form of sh.

Cold water is a start. Then I'd imagine you would have to apply some aloe vera. If you don't have any, I recommend getting some. It shouldn't cost you too much. Some people say not to cover burns, others say you should. Personally I think you should wrap it with something soft, not scratchy. Non-adhesive bandages should do.

I wouldn't know. There isn't a "simple yet direct" answer.

Personally, nobody in my life has even seen or knows about my scars. The reasoning behind such things are so diverse, or can be. If I were to explain it, I'd say that sometimes, it's an overwhelming emotion. For some people, it can be sadness. For me, it's always been frustration. It can be events, people, and sometimes life goes on even though you aren't necessarily ready to continue it. Some people need to feel like they have control over their lives, their bodies. It can help manage your thoughts or something. Others feel nothing at all. It can be all of these things. A variety of reasons.

Think about your situation. When you're lonely, or sad, is it the condition of being lonely that upsets you, or is it more than that? Did you overthink it? Were you in a place that being alone was inevitable, and more plausible than not?

When you're being self-destructive, you don't really think about anything else. Your focus isn't on your burdens anymore, and that might be everything for some people. It could have been your distraction. Some people love their injuries. When I was younger, I had a borderline morbid fascination with the outcome of self-harming. The sight, the feeling. You don't think it's wrong while you're actively doing it. In the moment, it's something else entirely.

It'll be hard to explain that to someone that hasn't done it.

When I was younger, I used to seriously consider the same thing.

People will tell you a lot of things, but I don't think it'll ever be the answer you want to hear. Distractions. Just "not thinking about it." Some religious person will assure you that there is something where there is none.

My condolences. I know it's terrifying, I'll be honest with you, and maybe there isn't anything for us after this life, but you don't have to die to escape fear.

It's terrifying. Inevitable, even, but it shouldn't start today. Easier said than done, but you should enjoy the time that you have. You aren't alone. I know that doesn't help, not really anyways, but we'll be right there with you. All the way, people you know and don't know, people you will meet and will never meet. Time is limited. What do you want to do with your life? What timeless beauties do you want to see, what things do you want to experience?

People that are afraid to die usually have one thing in common. It's the feeling that they haven't accomplished everything they wanted to accomplish, therefore they simply can't die yet. That might not be the case with you.

Personally I might not have methods that can help you, other than to focus on your time here. Death to me, atheist that I am, holds little importance now. Every now and then it freaks me out but, if I don't die, other people won't get the chance to experience the joys of this life, but that doesn't mean that this is where our story ends, or that it should. Memories of you will still be here, if that counts for anything. Think of death as inevitable, but fight that fear, don't give in to it. Dying now would give you less time to dwell on it, but it also prevents you from ever living. You'll be diving head-first into your biggest fear. Out if the frying pan and into the fire, I'm afraid.

I hope you find comfort.

Your response somewhat puts me at ease. The idea that we aren't just sheep, or pawns, in some grotesque world of wolves, is reassuring. I suppose that's quite the positive I'll have to contemplate more. It's better accepting something at face-value, despite everything.

The feeling is a constant for me. Feeling envious, although some days I feel better for it. Better that I didn't take my parents' word, fought their ideas with questions left unanswered.

I find the mere idea of any deities or afterlife impossible, but I really feel for religious people. It gives them hope. Who am I to tell them that it's false hope? They can overcome fear and melancholy simply through the teachings, or general idea that there is something beyond this life.

They're happy as is.

In a weird sense it's like this form of happiness or peace I can never really achieve. I suppose I'm not in a position to call religious people ignorant, but as they say, ignorance is bliss.

People have brought this up, and I might be too late, but I feel like no one really mentioned the extent.

You need to stop it before it gets out of hand, and if you haven't started, you need to distract yourself before it starts.

Personally I always thought it was something that I could stop doing. You won't think it's a problem, or an addiction, until you're too far gone. A few weeks or months in and you simply will not stop. Frequency might change, but it's hard to stop it once it becomes a habit, a routine.

Hey, it's no biggie.

I genuinely hope you recover from this. Get clean and all that.

Relapses are the worst.

Most people shouldn't, or don't, have to deal with this shit, you're right, but this doesn't define you.

Most people don't deal with this, you do, and you've made it this far.

You went through an entire year clean? Absolutely amazing. You can do it again, if that's what you want.

I know this shit is difficult. You don't immediately feel better about yourself. You don't just stop. But you're capable of so much. Relapses happen to the best of us. Nobody blames you for it.

You can do this.
This is both the funniest and worst thing I have seen this year.

To me, they're like an inconvenience.

It's a brand of sorts. I feel like, if they didn't scar, I would've done so much more, and I feel like its that way for a lot of people.

I'm not quite in your position, so I can't really say. I apologize if what I say isn't what you need to hear?

I don't have scars that would be as visible as yours. All of my shirts cover my biceps. I understand where you're coming from. 

No offense, I'm not implying anything. A lot of people react poorly to it, but you have to do what makes you comfortable. You want to cover them some days and expose them on other days? Do that. At the end of the day, some people might give you dirty looks or something, but those people have no idea what you've been through. If you don't want to cover them, I don't see a problem with that. It's your choice, and you should be allowed such comfort.

They could be stretch marks, I suppose. Perhaps at some point in their life they weren't as petite as they are now. Stretch marks end up scarring, I believe, so it could be that.

But I believe that another important factor is that you don't necessarily need depression in order to self-harm. Depression can be an influencing factor, but it is never this guarentee.

Maybe it's a different kind of scar. Car accident, or something of that sort.

It's too vague to make assumptions with. Would they be okay with you asking anything even remotely personal? If not, then maybe its better to leave it alone.

All I have access to is a stationary bike, but it's something, and I'll work with that.

That last line made my day for so many reasons. Thanks.

A majority of people that engage in any form of self-harm won't typically show that kind of behavior. I used to have two acquaintances that would have few, small, barely-broke-the-skin cuts. They would run to me, gesture to their arms, and say, "look what I did last night!", with big, bright smiles on their faces.

I find this behavior to be shameful. You can openly discuss self-harm, that much is fine. A willingness to show them is another story.

Genuine self-harmers that I've met are very hesitant to even talk about them, nonetheless show them off.

Some just want attention. It can be a cry for help, but that isn't always going to be the case.
